agent_response.response:
Generally, compensation for a cancelled one-way flight depends on the route, governing law, cancellation cause, notice period, and whether the airline offered reasonable rerouting—not on whether the ticket was one-way.

You may be entitled to:

- A refund of the unused flight or rerouting to your destination.
- Meals, lodging, and ground transportation during an extended disruption, depending on the jurisdiction.
- Fixed cash compensation where passenger-protection laws apply, unless the airline gave sufficient advance notice or the cancellation arose from extraordinary circumstances.
- Reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, with receipts.
- A travel credit or certificate as a goodwill remedy where statutory cash compensation does not apply.

Silver status usually does not increase statutory compensation. It may provide separate benefits such as priority rebooking, access to a dedicated support line, waived change fees, or an additional goodwill credit, depending on the airline’s program.

When contacting customer service, provide booking reference 00C256 and ask them to confirm the cancellation reason, notification date, applicable passenger-rights regime, refund or rerouting eligibility, expense reimbursement, and any Silver-tier goodwill benefit. Also provide a complete email address—“maya.chen.marketing” appears incomplete—so the certificate notification can be delivered.
